name: Martin Chen
life: “I once delivered Sunday bread in my daughter's decorated sports wagon.” People around the steps at Pier Beach know Martin by a small Saturday habit. Martin watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I delivered bread six mornings a week. On the seventh she ate with my family. I know the Sunday order.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and one cuff folded back twice. Martin has a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, with a neat white crop. Martin looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Martin has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To put the family's Sunday sandwich into the record.
family: Cora Yates is Martin’s younger cousin. Martin picks the meeting place. Cora sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The free fringe*, Cora says, “I gave up my slot because I remembered the first day I had nowhere to go before work.”
connections: Cynthia Moran. The delivery driver's Sunday version belongs on the card under the nickname the regular remembered.
